newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar gets boost from Euro currency worries.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar gets boost from Euro currency worries.

text.p: Fears that the German government's failure to carry the day in its row with the Bundesbank would lead to a weak single European currency prompted the dollar to zip higher on Wednesday.
Europe's main stock markets also booked gains in early trading, but government bond markets were unsettled over concerns about events in Germany and interest rate worries in Britain.

Although German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said he and the German central bank had agreed a common approach to revalue assets to help Bonn meet the economic targets for economic and monetary union (EMU), some of the details remained hazy.
Speaking to parliament, he did not make clear whether gold or currency reserves or both were to be revalued.
Waigel, who almost brought the government's relationship with the powerful Bundesbank to breaking point over his bid to revalue gold reserves, said no bullion would be sold to fill his budget gap.

But financial markets initially interpreted Bonn's climbdown on Tuesday as making its task of meeting EMU deficit goals tougher and increasing the risk of a broad number of EU countries joining what will be a soft euro currency.
"The government's backed down, the Bundesbank has won the round and now the Germans have to go back to the drawing board," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
But Waigel's declaration that Bonn remained committed to strict economic conditions for joining EMU hauled the mark off its lows.

The dollar was nearly a pfennig higher than late Tuesday rates at one point in early trading. But it had slipped back to about 1.7322 marks and 116.23 yen by 0915 GMT, slightly up on 116.06 yen seen in later European trade on Tuesday.
"The underlying tone of the dollar looks good, it's being helped by worries about the euro and should be supported by evidence of strong U.S. growth," said Stamenkovic.

Europe's major stock markets all showed good gains during the morning, with Paris clawing its way back from opening losses as the market waited for new Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to name his government.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 17.77 points, or 0.68 percent, at 2,642.26 at 0915 GMT as the market continued to recover following the Socialist election victory on Sunday.
A strong defensive play with buying in the oil, food and retail sectors has helped pushed the market higher, one broker said.

Oil major Elf Aquitaine rose 1.29 percent to 627 francs, having risen strongly since last Friday's forecast of 35 percent first-half pre-exceptional profit growth. "Elf is definitely pulling the market," one broker said.
Leading British shares snapped a five-day losing streak with a small bounce at the opening, getting support from a firm close on Wall Street where the Dow ended up 22 points.
By mid-morning, the benchmark FTSE 100 was up 19.3 points at 4,577.1, having closed at a four-week low on Tuesday.
Yet any recovery in the British share market was likely to be limited, dealers said.

"There are still so many uncertainties surrounding this market ... We have uncertainty about rates, the budget and EMU and I don't think we can gain too much ground until some of these uncertainties are put to rest," said one dealer.

The Bank of England is set for its first monetary meeting as an independent entity on Friday. Dealers said that if the central bank did not raise interest rates this week, then rates were almost certainly poised to rise later this summer.
Also on Friday, the United States will report key jobs data, which are seen as the best indication of the course of U.S. monetary policy.
In Frankfurt, Germany's 30-share DAX index played catch up in early bourse trade to match gains in electronic screen trade late on Tuesday.
By 0915 GMT the DAX was showing gains of 35 points, or nearly one percent, with the dollar, debt market and Wall Street's overnight close underpinning sentiment.
The soothing words from both sides on the Bundesbank-Bonn gold revaluation row were seen as mostly market neutral.
CURRENCIES AT 0915 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7322 marks and 116.32 yen compared with 1.7263 marks and 116.06 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0915 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 19.3 points, or 0.42 percent, at 4,577.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 17.77 points, or 0.68 percent, at 2,642.26.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 35.66 points, or 0.98 percent, at 3,661.4.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed easier at $342.55 versus $343.55 on Tuesday afternoon and a $342.85 close. Platinum was fixed at a new 16-month high of $425.00, while palladium fixed at highest-ever level of $210.00. Silver was up a cent at $4.75.
